source: FAO Plant Production and Protection Division — Rice cultivation (illustrative smallholder guide)
spacing: Transplant 2–3 seedlings per hill, 20 cm × 20 cm in puddled fields.
how_to_grow: Prepare nursery beds and sow pre-germinated seed. Transplant 21–25-day-old seedlings into a puddled, level field. Maintain 5–10 cm standing water during early growth, then alternate wetting and drying in many systems. Weed within the first 30 days after transplanting.
harvest_signs: Harvest when 80–85% of grains on the panicle are golden yellow and firm. Cut at 20–25 cm above ground if threshing by hand. Dry grain to 14% moisture for safe storage.

stages.name: Nursery
stages.watering: Keep nursery beds flooded or very moist; protect from heavy rain on young seedlings.
stages.nutrients: Apply a small dose of nitrogen in the nursery only if seedlings look pale — follow local extension rates.

stages.name: Tillering
stages.watering: Maintain shallow flood or saturated soil; drain briefly if algae or pests build up.
stages.nutrients: Basal nitrogen and phosphorus at transplant; split nitrogen applications per local recommendation.

stages.name: Panicle initiation
stages.watering: Do not let the field dry completely during this sensitive stage.
stages.nutrients: Second nitrogen split before panicle initiation; ensure potassium if soils are deficient.

stages.name: Grain filling
stages.watering: Gradual drainage in many varieties improves grain filling and reduces lodging.
stages.nutrients: Late nitrogen only if extension advises; excess late N increases lodging.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.watering: Drain field fully 7–10 days before harvest.
stages.nutrients: No feeding; harvest at correct moisture.
